reason: First reassessment in two weeks. The defensive risk-premia book is doing its job: +1.35% with a -2.39% max drawdown against a tape where 75% of S&P stocks fell in September, and no leg's thesis is invalidated by its mark. The two losing legs, GLD (-4.6%) and TLT (-4.9%, 5% weight, -8% stop), were hit by the same factor, the five-week bond rout that took the 10-year to 5.34% on 10-01 after the Fed's 09-16 hike; Friday's +29k payroll miss and 4.2% unemployment flipped CME odds to ~80% for an October hold, yields fell and the dollar dropped, which is precisely the turn both contrarian legs were sized for, so selling them now would be selling at the point of maximum pressure. EWZ (7%, +0.3%) faces Brazil's first round on Sunday 10-04, which resolves before any order I write could execute at the 10-05 close; the leg already carries the pre-election -12% stop and +10% take-profit, Brazil's fear gauge is at a record 31.8 so a lot is priced, and prediction markets (Flavio ~57%) versus polls (runoff tied) give no edge to pre-empt. UNH (-1.5%) reports 10-13 with pre-earnings caution already in the price and a 30% stop for a contrarian-value leg; BRK-B is flat with Howard Buffett now chair and Abel as CEO, business as usual; SVXY (+0.9%) is fine with VIX at 15.3 and a quiet week ahead (ISM services, FOMC minutes). No change I would make is worth more than the noise of making it, and the book keeps 46% cash at 4% to absorb the Brazil and UNH events. Zero overlap with the Round 2 momentum book is preserved.
